tagline: Understand contribution paths after an event
introText: Follow a cohort over time, on its original projects and across the Wikimedia ecosystem.

aboutText: Wikimedia Retention is a free and open source tool for analyzing contribution paths after an event. This independent project is not an official service of the Wikimedia Foundation.
sourceCode: Project and source code on GitHub
exportHelp: JSON: a complete backup you can import to restore the collection. PDF: a report with results, charts and methodology, with optional individual account details. CSV: tables you can use in Excel or LibreOffice.
saveHelp: The collection stays in memory during this visit. Export the JSON before closing or reloading the page. PDF and CSV files cannot restore the analysis. No collection library is stored on the server.
matrixNote: A person may appear in several destinations. Original projects are those declared for the event, not an observed individual journey.
noData: Import a cohort and collect its contributions to display results.
nominative: Include individual account details in the PDF

csvHeader: The CSV has a header row
limit: An imported cohort can contain up to {{maximum}} accounts.
saved: Analysis imported without new contribution requests.
qualificationNote: Review the list and check the accounts to exclude. “Verify accounts and continue” confirms that accounts exist, retrieves their creation dates and detects bots. It updates the table, then opens Settings. This verification does not collect their contributions yet.
timelineLimit: The latest 100 edits in the selected period are shown here. The JSON export preserves all collected data.
collectionNotice: Collection retrieves contributions after the event through the analysis date, across the selected projects. Choose deadlines, languages and edit types in Results. You can pause or cancel collection.
methodText: Sources are CentralAuth for global and local accounts, Programs & Events Dashboard for public programs and roles, the MediaWiki APIs for public revisions and namespaces, and XTools Global Contributions for sequential global collection. No private key is required.

Dates are interpreted in UTC and calendar days. The event includes its start and end dates. Day +1 is the day after the event ends. The reference date is fixed when collection starts. Dashboard dates may cover an entire program and must be checked for the event being studied.

A new account has a global creation date within the window around the event start, including both boundaries. “Everyone” includes all accounts not excluded, regardless of their creation date. “New accounts only” includes accounts not excluded within that window; accounts with unknown dates cannot be included in that selection.

A person is counted once they have made at least one edit in the selected period. J+30 covers the day after the event ends through day 30 inclusive. This total does not mean the person is still contributing on the final day.

Rates use included and filtered participants. If an included participant has incomplete collection, observed counts remain visible but final rates are unavailable. A failure is never treated as certain inactivity. Results do not establish a causal link between training and later contributions.

The taxonomy uses canonical namespace names, their family and the specific project. Talk pages belong to community. Commons files belong to media. Wikidata entities belong to structured data. On Wikisource, Page is content and Index is maintenance. Rules are documented in the YAML file.

Bots are detected from explicit global or local groups, never from usernames. Known tags or the bot flag identify some automated edits. XTools does not always provide these markers. A missing marker does not guarantee a fully manual edit.

Global collection depends on public revisions and supported projects. Public archived revision metadata for Wikipedia articles is collected separately; hidden data remains inaccessible. Unattached local accounts, renames and replica lag may limit coverage.

Cohorts are not stored in a remote database or saved permanently by this application. Data stays in browser memory. Account verification and contribution requests pass through the backend without logging request bodies or usernames. Exporting JSON is a voluntary backup. PDF reports are aggregated by default.

Included people who made at least one edit in the period, by project family. A person may contribute on several projects. Percentages use all included participants, so they may add up to more than 100%.
resetHelp: Starting a new analysis will clear the current participants, settings and results. Any collection in progress will stop. Save a JSON backup first if you want to keep this analysis.
creationHelp: Day 0 is the event start date. Day -14 to Day 0 includes accounts created from 14 days before the start to the start day, inclusive. Older accounts stay outside this selection. To choose another window, enter both dates using “Custom period”.
creationSummary: Accounts created between {{before}} days before and {{after}} days after the event start will be considered new.
allSelectionHelp: All accounts that are not excluded from the participant list are included, regardless of their creation date.
newSelectionHelp: Only accounts created within the window below are included, among accounts not excluded. Accounts created before or after this window are not included even if they participated in the event. Choose “Everyone” to follow them too. Unknown creation dates do not yet allow an account to be included.
participantCounts: {{total}} accounts imported: {{included}} not excluded and {{excluded}} excluded.
excludeHelp: Check “Yes” to select an exclusion, then confirm with “Apply selected exclusions”. Automatic exclusions for organizers and bots can be changed.
resultsCoverage: Included accounts: {{retained}}. Fully collected accounts: {{complete}}. Accounts to complete: {{pending}}. Collection progress is independent of the deadline chosen for the results.
newResultsHelp: New account selection depends on account creation dates. Accounts without a known date stay in the backup file but are not included in this calculation.
automationHelp: Removes edits flagged as made by a bot or an automated tool, such as AutoWikiBrowser, from calculations. Detection depends on information supplied by the sources and does not identify all automation.

categoryExamples.CONTENT: Creating and editing Wikipedia articles, Wikisource texts or content pages on other projects.
categoryExamples.STRUCTURED_DATA: Editing Wikidata items, properties or lexemes.
categoryExamples.MEDIA: Editing file pages on Commons, such as descriptions or licenses. This count does not cover all uploads.
categoryExamples.MAINTENANCE: Editing categories, templates, modules or help pages.
categoryExamples.COMMUNITY: Messages and edits on article or user talk pages.
categoryExamples.OTHER: Other namespaces, such as user pages and drafts that do not fall into the categories above.

verificationProgress: Verification: {{done}} accounts out of {{total}}. Creation dates and exclusions are being updated in the table.
verificationSummary: Verification complete. Verified accounts: {{verified}}. Accounts excluded from the analysis: {{excluded}}. Creation dates are available in the imported list. You can now configure collection.
verificationIncomplete: Verification is still incomplete for {{count}} accounts that are not excluded. Retry with “Verify accounts and continue”. No contributions have been collected yet.
verificationIncomplete_one: Verification is still incomplete for {{count}} account that is not excluded. Retry with “Verify accounts and continue”. No contributions have been collected yet.
verificationIncomplete_other: Verification is still incomplete for {{count}} accounts that are not excluded. Retry with “Verify accounts and continue”. No contributions have been collected yet.
pdfUntilReference: Up to the reference date: {{count}} people observed as active.
fallbackSummary: XTools did not respond for {{count}} accounts. Collection uses the Wikimedia APIs as a fallback for these accounts. Data already collected is preserved.
periodHelp: Each value is the share of included participants with at least one contribution during that interval, counted after the event ends. For example, Day +31 to Day +90 covers the 31st to the 90th day. Each person is counted once per period.
cumulativeHelp: Each value is the share of included participants with at least one contribution from the day after the event ends until that deadline. It does not mean they are still contributing on that date.
migrationHelp: Each included person is counted once, according to the projects they contributed to after the event. Original projects are those selected in Settings.
projectHelp: Number of eligible creations or edits after the event, by project. One person can make several contributions. Percentages show the share of observed contributions.
monthlyHelp: Number of eligible contributions each month after the event, not the number of people. The current month is incomplete. Percentages show the share of observed contributions.
natureHelp: Eligible contributions after the event by category. Percentages show the share of observed contributions.
currentCumulative: As of {{date}}, {{active}} out of {{total}} participants have contributed at least once since the event ended: {{rate}}%. This cumulative total does not measure activity on that single day.
currentCumulativePartial: As of {{date}}, at least {{active}} out of {{total}} participants have contributed since the event ended. Incomplete collection prevents a final rate.
creationDates: Accounts considered new: created from {{start}} to {{end}}, inclusive.
selectionPreview: Selection before collection: {{selected}} included accounts out of {{total}} accounts not excluded. Creation dates still unknown: {{unknown}}.
zeroSelection: No account matches this selection. Check the event start and creation window, or choose “Everyone”. Collection cannot start with zero included participants.
dashboardDateCheck: Dates supplied by the Dashboard: {{start}} to {{end}} (UTC). They may cover an entire program rather than this event.
noParticipantsResults: No participant matches the current filters. Data is preserved. Return to Settings to check the event dates, new account window and exclusions.
participantTableHelp: “Contributions after the event” counts eligible creations or edits observed for each account, even when excluded from the summary. Charts and totals use only included participants.
confirmEventDates: Confirm or replace the event dates supplied by the Dashboard before collection.
eventDatesHelp: Enter the event start and end here, before collection. For a one-day event, enter the same date in both fields. These dates apply only to this analysis: the Dashboard stays unchanged and no administrator access is needed. Contributions will be tracked after the event ends up to today.
dashboardDatesQuestion: Do the Dashboard dates match the event?
customEventDates: No, enter the actual dates below
futureDashboardDates: The supplied end date is in the future. Enter the actual event dates below.

fup.title: How many people contributed after the event?
fup.help: A person is counted once they have made at least one edit in the selected period. J+30 covers the day after the event ends through day 30 inclusive. This total does not mean the person is still contributing on the final day.
fup.deadline: How far after the event should we look?
fup.deadlineHelp: If J+X falls after today, choose “Today” to avoid errors.
fup.customDays: Custom number of days after the event ends
fup.invalid: Enter a whole number of days between 1 and 36,500 and check the event dates.
fup.projects: Projects to look for contributions on
fup.projectHelp: Choose Wikipedia languages separately alongside. Other families include all their languages.
fup.languageHelp: Select editions relevant to your group, such as Breton, Occitan or Alsatian. The catalogue contains available Wikipedia editions.
fup.languageSearch: Search for a language or its code
fup.categoriesHelp: By default, only article creation and editing are counted on Wikipedia. Add discussions or maintenance if they are relevant to your question.
fup.otherCategories: All edit categories are counted on Commons, Wikidata and the other selected projects. The automated edit exclusion follows your collection settings.
fup.noProjects: No available project matches your choices. Select at least one project and, for Wikipedia, a language.
fup.notReached: The selected period ends on {{date}}, but collected data stops on {{observed}}. Contributions already observed are shown, without a definitive result for that deadline. Choose “Today” for the available results, then complete collection if the data is old.
fup.futureDeadline: The selected period ends on {{date}}: this deadline is still in the future. Contributions are shown through {{observed}}, without a definitive result for that deadline. Choose “Today” for the available results.
fup.missingScope: Your question also includes projects outside the collection scope. Choose only projects already collected in these results, or complete collection across all projects.
fup.changedCollection: Dates or projects have changed since the last collection. Run collection with these settings to complete the results. Contributions already retrieved are kept.
fup.collectionUnavailable_one: One account’s contributions could not be fully retrieved from public services. The account remains included. Resume collection to complete its data; no observed contribution does not mean the account made no edits.
fup.collectionClassification_one: One account’s contributions were retrieved, but the information needed to classify its page types is unavailable. Resume collection to complete classification. Retrieved contributions are kept.
fup.collectionClassification_other: Contributions for {{count}} accounts were retrieved, but the information needed to classify their page types is unavailable. Resume collection to complete classification. Retrieved contributions are kept.
fup.collectionUnavailable_other: Contributions for {{count}} accounts could not be fully retrieved from public services. These accounts remain included. Resume collection to complete their data; no observed contribution does not mean they made no edits.
fup.collectionUnverified_one: One included account could not be verified. Go back to Import to check its existence before collecting its contributions.
fup.collectionUnverified_other: {{count}} included accounts could not be verified. Go back to Import to check their existence before collecting their contributions.
fup.collectionUnfinished_one: Collection is not finished for one included account. Its contributions have not yet been fully checked. Resume collection to finish its analysis.
fup.collectionUnfinished_other: Collection is not finished for {{count}} included accounts. Their contributions have not yet been fully checked. Resume collection to finish their analysis.
fup.answer: {{active}} out of {{total}} people made at least one edit in this period, or {{rate}}%.
fup.minimum: {{active}} out of {{total}} people have already made at least one edit in the observed period.
fup.activityHelp: Each included person is counted once. “No contribution” requires complete collection; other accounts without an observed contribution remain under “Insufficient data”.
fup.projectTitle: How many people contribute on each project?
fup.familyHelp: Included people who made at least one observed edit in the period, by project family. The observed share is this count divided by all included participants. It may increase if the period or collection is not complete. A person may contribute on several projects, so these percentages may add up to more than 100%.
fup.tableHelp: This list shows people with at least one edit in the period and projects selected above. Click a name to open their details. Show all accounts to view other participants or undo an exclusion.
fup.tableCaption: Individual contributions in the selected period
fup.renameHelp: Tracking follows imported accounts. A rename normally preserves the global account, but this tool does not automatically resolve name changes. A separate new account must be added manually; the APIs cannot prove it belongs to the same person.
fup.exportHelp: CSV and PDF use the period, projects and filters shown here. JSON saves the entire analysis, collected data and selected question for later use. The PDF omits names by default.
fup.filters: Wikipedia languages: {{languages}}. Wikipedia edit types: {{categories}}. Other projects: all categories.
fup.publicHistoryHelp: These links open a new tab with all public edits by this account on each project, since its first edits. This history extends beyond the period selected in this analysis.
fup.emptyList: No accounts match this view. Choose “All imported accounts” or change the period, projects and search.

resultsFiltersHelp: Choose deadlines and edit types in Results. Commons, Wikidata and other projects count all edit categories there.
invalidCreationRange: Enter a valid creation window, with the start on or before the end and no future date.
projectPickerHelp: Open a project family, then select the languages or sites to collect. Search by language, language code or project name.
selectionReviewTitle: View included accounts and reasons for non-selection
selectionReviewHelp: This list explains the current filter. An account outside the creation window remains in the import: choose “Everyone” to follow it, or adjust the window.
selectionExcluded: Account excluded in the participant list.
selectionNeedsStart: Enter the event start to calculate the window.
selectionNeedsVerification: The account creation date or existence could not yet be verified.
selectionCreatedBefore: Account created before the selected window.
selectionCreatedAfter: Account created after the selected window.
exclusionsPending: Selection not applied. Confirm exclusions before continuing.
exclusionsHelp: Select accounts to exclude, then apply the selection before continuing.

deleted.title: Contributions to subsequently deleted articles
deleted.includeCreations: Include creations of subsequently deleted articles
deleted.includeModifications: Include edits to subsequently deleted articles
deleted.help: These records are searched during collection on the observed Wikipedia editions. The checkboxes immediately recalculate results without new requests. Reverted edits on existing articles remain counted.
deleted.counts: In the period, before these exclusions: {{creations}} deleted creations and {{modifications}} archived edits retrieved.
deleted.unknown: {{count}} archived contributions could not yet be identified as creations or edits. They remain included while at least one checkbox is selected.
deleted.incomplete: Archived contribution collection could not finish for {{count}} accounts. Results including them remain a minimum.
deleted.classificationIncomplete: The deleted creation source did not respond. Separately excluding creations or edits cannot yet provide a definitive rate.
deleted.oldArchive: This analysis does not yet contain the additional archived contribution collection. Restart collection to retrieve it. The checkboxes only affect records already retrieved.

topics.title: Topics of articles created on Wikipedia, beta
topics.deleted: {{count}} deleted articles are included in the counts without an available topic. These articles are not sent to the model. Their contributions follow the two inclusion checkboxes in the results.
topics.partial: The period or collection is incomplete. These statistics describe only the contributions already observed.
topics.intro: Created articles are shown by default. You can also select edited articles. Wikimedia’s outlink-topic-model is only called for accessible articles in the selection.
topics.method: outlink-topic-model is Wikimedia’s multilingual model, available through Lift Wing. It uses fastText and article links mapped to Wikidata to estimate 64 topics. We retain confidence scores of at least 0.5.
topics.methodLimits: It classifies the article at analysis time, not the text added. Topics may overlap or be missing. Classification is indicative; scores are not percentages of contributions. JSON preserves the classification for reuse.
topics.empty: No Wikipedia article contributions in the current selection. Check the selected projects, languages and page types.
topics.period: This analysis follows the period, accounts, projects and filters selected above. Only Wikipedia’s main namespace is included. Pausing keeps examined articles in this page; JSON saves them after a pause or at completion.
topics.answer: Contributing accounts: {{contributors}} of {{total}} retained accounts ({{rate}}). Distinct articles: {{articles}}. Observed contributions: {{edits}}.
topics.volumeCaption: Article contributions before the creation or edit filter
topics.unknownType: Older analyses may lack creation flags. Examining articles fills this information where public history allows it. Undetermined types remain in the total and are not treated as edits to existing articles.

base.contributors: Percentages use the {{count}} contributors to the selected articles.
base.articles: Percentages use the {{count}} distinct articles in the selection.
base.edits: Percentages use the {{count}} contributions in the selection.

topics.overlap: An article may have several topics. Each unit counts once per topic; percentages may sum to more than 100%.
topics.coverage: Classified articles: {{classified}} of {{total}} ({{rate}}). No recognised topic: {{unclassified}}. Source unavailable: {{unavailable}}. To examine: {{pending}}.
topics.unavailable: The public source did not respond for some articles. Their contributions remain in the total. Use ‘Complete topic analysis’ to retry.
topics.excluded: {{count}} pages are excluded from the article totals (redirects, disambiguations or pages inaccessible today).
topics.noThemes: No topics available for this selection. Complete the analysis or change the filter.

newAccounts.title: New registrations on French Wikipedia
newAccounts.intro: Build a cohort from the public account creation log.
newAccounts.creationDates: 1. Which accounts do you want to follow?
newAccounts.history: Inclusive dates, in UTC. This module supports the log from 18 April 2006. The older format is not supported. Hidden or deleted data is unavailable.
newAccounts.exclusions: IPs, temporary accounts and automatic attachments of existing accounts are excluded. Renamed accounts are looked up by ID when available.
newAccounts.invalidDates: Choose a date or range between 18 April 2006 and today.
newAccounts.failed: Loading stopped. Resume to continue from the same point.
newAccounts.unavailable: {{count}} log entries could not be associated with a public account. They are outside the analysable cohort, so this list is not exhaustive.
newAccounts.browser: Keep this page open while loading. You can pause and resume. After import, save the analysis JSON to resume later.
newAccounts.existingGlobal: The global account already existed before this local registration.
newAccounts.cohortDates: Accounts created on French Wikipedia from {{start}} through {{end}}.
newAccounts.observationHelp: You follow the same accounts after registration. Choose an end date or a date range in which to count their contributions.

mode.registration: From each account’s registration until a date
mode.period: Within a date range after each account’s registration

modeHelp.registration: Contributions count from each account’s registration through the chosen end date, inclusive.
modeHelp.period: Choose a start date and an end date. Only contributions within this range count, after each account’s registration.

scope.custom: Custom selection by project and language

newAccounts.automationHelp: Accounts identified as bots are excluded by default. This checkbox, enabled by default, also excludes edits flagged as bot or automated made by other accounts.
newAccounts.preparationProgress: Finding contribution projects: {{done}} of {{total}} accounts examined.
newAccounts.progressRefresh: Counters refresh every two seconds. A public source request may take longer.
newAccounts.durationInfo: Info: allow roughly 17 minutes to examine the contribution projects of 1,000 accounts, plus extra time to retrieve their edits. This is an indicative estimate and depends on API response times.
newAccounts.fileLimit: TXT and CSV files up to 50 MB are accepted.
newAccounts.allProjects: {{count}} public catalogue projects will be observed, across all their languages. Only projects where the account has contributions are queried.
newAccounts.report: Among the {{total}} retained accounts created on French Wikipedia from {{start}} through {{end}}, {{active}} ({{rate}}%) made at least one eligible edit {{period}}. This represents {{edits}} observed edits.
newAccounts.reportPartial: Among the {{total}} retained accounts created on French Wikipedia from {{start}} through {{end}}, at least {{active}} made an eligible edit {{period}}. {{unknown}} accounts do not yet have a definitive conclusion.
newAccounts.reportHelp: An eligible edit matches the selected projects and types. An account may appear on several projects but is counted once overall. Accounts with no edits remain in the cohort. This measure does not demonstrate continuous activity.
newAccounts.collectionNotice: Choose the observation interval and projects. Contribution type filters apply only to Wikipedia. Collection can be paused and resumed.
newAccounts.txtImported: List restored: accounts created from {{start}} through {{end}}. TXT preserves usernames. Use the cohort CSV to also restore registration dates and the dedicated flow.

wikipediaExamples.MAINTENANCE: Editing categories, templates, modules or help pages.

newAccounts.activityTitle: Which accounts contributed during this period?
newAccounts.activityHelp: Each retained account counts once. No contribution is confirmed only when collection is complete.
newAccounts.projectTitle: How many accounts contribute on each project?
newAccounts.familyHelp: Accounts with at least one edit, by project family. Percentages use all retained accounts as the denominator. An account may contribute on several projects.
